text: Observed in jigwright-package-side (6a21f4b) while recording pilot findings. The private Finding store and the Governance Source ledger both hold agent observations, and which one a caller can use is decided by whether a session happens to be open rather than by what the record says. Two concrete facts: the Finding record carries sessionId, changeId, branch, head, tree, text and sourceRefs but no author field, so maintainer wording produced in the middle of a task has no private staging path at all, while later and attach write the committed ledger that a task-scoped agent may not touch; and finding add resolves its session through loadActiveSessionContext, which requires a session file in runtime.sessions whose state is active, so recording this very observation through the Finding path failed with INVALID_SESSION_ID and it was captured as an agent Source instead, exactly as the eight earlier pilot findings were. Neither repository has ever held a single Finding. The proposed model separates two things the current design fuses: authorship stays maintainer or agent as it already is on a Source, and publication state becomes private staging or committed ledger, available to both authors. Session, branch, head and tree become evidence fields on a staged record rather than a separate artifact type. This also gives mid-task requirement changes a path they currently lack.
